text:
maria: Heads up — users reported that permalinks to headings inside a collapsed sidebar section no longer scroll to the heading on the page. Only happens when the sidebar group is collapsed. Repro: open /docs/guide, click link to `#using-the-cache` and nothing happens.

raj: saw this in the wild too. It seems related to how we normalize anchors for collapsible sidebar headings vs page slugs. Docusaurus adds ids like `using-the-cache` but the sidebar adds a prefix when collapsed?

kevin: can you paste a failing link?

maria: sure — link format that fails: `https://docs.redwood.inference.dev/docs/guide#using-the-cache`. When the group is collapsed the DOM id is still there, but scrollIntoView doesn't run because the sidebar JS intercepts hashchange and tries to expand the group, then loses the focus.

raj: minimal repro in console: run `window.location.hash = '#using-the-cache'` — if the sidebar is closed nothing happens. If you manually expand the group then it works.

docsbot: linkcheck job failed on deploy-preview #3345:
```
WARN  Link check: /docs/guide -> #using-the-cache (404 on client-side navigation)
```

kevin: opened a spike branch: docs/anchor-sidebar-fix. My plan: when handling `hashchange`, first expand the sidebar group (if needed) and then call `document.getElementById(hash)` after a short microtask so scroll happens reliably. Patch includes a small debounce.

sophia: sounds good. can you drop the PR? we need to backport into `v2` branch before the release tomorrow.

kevin: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1428 (WIP). Diff summary: update `sidebar.js` handler, add unit test for `expandAndScroll(hash)`, and add a note to migration guide about anchor id normalization for older mkdocs pages.

maria: +1 for tests. also found a handful of pages where code block indentation created bogus header ids — e.g., in `docs/examples/streaming.md` we had an indented heading that generated `streaming-1` instead of `streaming`. I added explicit header ID on that page as a quick fix: `### Streaming example {#streaming}`.

raj: can we add a small validation step in the CI linkcheck that rejects duplicate generated ids? Might be heavy but useful.

kevin: added a fast sanity check script in the PR: `scripts/check-duplicate-ids.js` that emits warnings and fails on duplicates in a single markdown file. Run with `node scripts/check-duplicate-ids.js docs/`. Would you prefer fail vs warn?

sophia: fail on duplicates for `main` and `v2` branches. warn for personal branches. avoids regressions.

maria: also adding a docs note in the migration guide: "if your headings are indented under fenced code or lists, use explicit `{#id}` to ensure stable anchors across builds."

raj: reviewed the JS, left 2 small comments re: clearing timeouts and avoiding layout thrash.

kevin: addressed comments, PTAL. Added `await tick()` util that uses `Promise.resolve().then()` instead of setTimeout.

docsbot: CI: test/linkcheck — failed on preview because the handler wasn't in the built static assets for the deploy-preview.

kevin: pushed fix to ensure the handler is imported in the client entry. CI now green on my branch.

sophia: i'll do the `v2` backport after you merge. please add a clear changelog entry.

maria: chore: mention that this also fixes deep-links from external sites (we saw one customer report).

deploy-bot: deploy-preview #3345 updated — staging link: https://deploy-preview-3345--docs.redwood.inference.dev/docs/guide#using-the-cache

raj: tested in staging. clicking the permalink now expands the sidebar and scrolls correctly. :tada:

kevin: merging PR now. will open backport PR to `v2` with the same tests.

sophia: thanks all — nice triage and quick turnaround. I'll include the fix in the release notes: "Fix: permalink scrolling when sidebar groups are collapsed (docs)"

maria: resolved — will close the related support ticket after backport is merged. :white_check_mark:
